title: APEC members reached consensus on safe AI use, China’s Chen Xu says
excerpt: Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) members are focusing on the safe deployment and responsible use of AI, a senior Chinese official said on Tuesday, Reuters reported. content_html:
Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) members are focusing on the safe deployment and responsible use of AI, a senior Chinese official said on Tuesday, Reuters reported.

Chen Xu, China’s former ambassador to the UN, chairs this year’s APEC Senior Officials’ Meeting. He told a press conference that members had held in-depth talks on AI and reached an important consensus, according to Reuters. He did not give details of what was agreed.

“The parties engaged in in-depth discussions on a wide range of issues,” Chen said of digital technology and AI.

China is hosting APEC this year. The leaders’ meeting takes place in Shenzhen on 18 and 19 November. Chen said on Tuesday that China wants an ambitious outcome document from the meeting, China Daily reported.

AI has been on APEC’s agenda all year. In July, members adopted a statement on AI at a digital and AI ministerial meeting in Chengdu. It set out a framework for regional cooperation on AI development.

The push builds on last year’s summit in South Korea. There, Chinese President Xi Jinping proposed a global body to govern AI, Reuters reported at the time. He also said AI would be on the agenda when China hosted APEC in 2026.

APEC has 21 member economies, including the US and China.
